builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Multimodal Routing and Region Refinement for Language-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
summary: MRSeg replaces single-pathway fine-tuning of vision-language segmentation models with a shared sparse router over low-rank adapter bases applied to frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny and PubMedBERT encoders, plus a region-refinement module before dense decoding. The cost is architectural complexity: router training stability, adapter bank design, and a custom decoder, though the 7.11M trainable parameter count and 7.60 GFLOPs fit comfortably within a 24 GB GPU budget. Failure modes include router collapse to a few adapter bases, degraded generalization to modalities or text styles outside the two evaluation datasets, and limited transfer if the reader's workload is not medical image segmentation.
rationale: The method is computationally feasible on constrained infrastructure and the parameter-efficient routing idea may transfer to other vision-language tasks, but its value is demonstrated only on two small medical segmentation benchmarks, so workload-specific validation is required before adoption.
technique: Routed low-rank adapters for text-guided medical segmentation

claims.statement: MRSeg replaces single-pathway fine-tuning of vision-language segmentation models with a shared sparse router over low-rank adapter bases applied to frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny and PubMedBERT encoders, plus a region-refinement module before dense decoding. The cost is architectural complexity: router training stability, adapter bank design, and a custom decoder, though the 7.11M trainable parameter count and 7.60 GFLOPs fit comfortably within a 24 GB GPU budget. Failure modes include router collapse to a few adapter bases, degraded generalization to modalities or text styles outside the two evaluation datasets, and limited transfer if the reader's workload is not medical image segmentation.
Reports 90.90/83.32 Dice/mIoU on QaTa-COV19 and 81.53/68.82 on MosMedData+ with 7.11M trainable parameters and 7.60 GFLOPs; no multiplicative speedup or memory factor is claimed against a baseline.
